_rule: R-TERM-01 — a terminal's maintenance capital rests on a DISCLOSED useful life. engine/terminal_value.py refuses one this desk chose (SIGCM clause 1).
_source: ADNOC L&S FY2025 annual report, note on property, plant and equipment: 'Depreciation is calculated using the straight-line method to allocate the assets' costs to their residual values over their estimated useful lives as follows'.
_route: text layer (pdftotext -layout, 846,805 characters extracted). No OCR needed; the figures foot against the same table in the prior-year report.
review_policy: estimated useful lives, residual values and depreciation method are reviewed ANNUALLY, with the effect of any change accounted for prospectively.

adopted_for_terminal.basis: the fleet, which is the asset base
adopted_for_terminal.reasoning: ADNOC L&S is a shipping and logistics group and its terminal capital base is its fleet. Tankers, dry-bulk and containers are disclosed at 25 years exactly; offshore vessels at 20-25 and gas carriers at 25-40 bracket it. Plant is 20. The 50-year figure in the buildings range belongs to ports and land improvements, which are not what a replacement-cost fleet base measures.
adopted_for_terminal.what_would_overturn_it: a disclosed breakdown of property, plant and equipment BY COST showing the base is dominated by ports and land improvements rather than by vessels; or a later filing revising these lives, which management reviews annually and accounts for prospectively.
adopted_for_terminal.the_finding: The study's terminal implies a replacement cycle of 1/g = 50 years, because its terminal growth is 2.0%. Against a disclosed fleet life of 25 years it UNDER-CHARGES MAINTENANCE BY EXACTLY 2.00x, worth about -16.6% of enterprise value. THIS IS THE MODEL REPORT — the exemplar every study in this book is written against — and the error runs the OPPOSITE way to the pessimism this reassessment was called over, which is what makes it worth reporting rather than convenient to find.
